column1: # The one floating-point contract for every Laplace build: Native, Engine, PostgreSQL, PostGIS and every dependency,
# on Linux and Windows. The same input gives the same bits on every machine.
# Read by toolchain/laplace.cmake (CMake), and by setup.sh and setup.ps1 for Meson native files and autotools CFLAGS.
# Columns: what (compile, link, nobuiltin), driver (gnu: icx/icpx/icx-cc; msvc: icx-cl on Windows; any), value.
# A nobuiltin row is a libm function: the compiler may not fold it at build time with the build host's libm, turn it
# into an SVML vector call or a vendor intrinsic; every call reaches laplace-math (core-math, correctly rounded).
# Measured with icx 2026.1.1 on both machines (2026-10-04): the default is fast math, FMA contraction and SVML; the
# precise flags remove those but cos(0.5) is still folded at build time until -fno-builtin-cos; on Linux an icx-built
# object links libimf and libsvml unless -no-intel-lib.
# Windows keeps libmmd for exact operations only (sqrt, round, fmin/fmax, ldexp, the fenv calls): icx's headers
# declare those as imports from it, and the UCRT defines feraiseexcept only inline. The transcendental functions are
# plain calls, and laplace-math comes first on the link line, so none reaches libmmd; the fingerprint's override
# x86-64-v3 is what both machines have (i7-6850K Broadwell-E, i9-14900KS; neither has AVX-512). With contraction and
# reassociation off, vectorizing does not change results, so the ISA level is speed only.
